reason: Conversation 1 kept the diagnosis honest: it correctly explained that a lit spur neon does not prove power is reaching the dishwasher, told the owner to isolate at the consumer unit before touching the fuse drawer, and when the owner could not check the fuse it escalated cleanly with the useful instruction to have the engineer test the spur output before condemning any dishwasher parts. Conversation 2 was more thorough on practical detail (door-open control check on integrated Neff, how to swap a fuse, warranty, model number) but made an unsupported claim that 'the neon is after the fuse so the fuse is usually fine', effectively ruling out one of the genuinely possible causes, and padded the thread with repeated resets, a hunt for a hypothetical plug, and speculative part names (power module, mains filter). Conversation 1 could have offered a cheaper path to a known-good 13A fuse rather than going straight to an engineer, which keeps the margin slight.
